_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
EVERY FIELD HAS A WORD CAP, and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build past it:
name 16, why 40, risk 80, touches 80, note 120, comment 120, askedBy.detail 80. A
session with more to say than that puts it in the feature's Brief or history file
and links it. ONE FACT, ONE HOME: replace a sentence that is out of date; never append
an UPDATED paragraph beneath it. On 2026-09-03 one item's comment had grown to 1,388
words across seven sessions that way, and Mike could not read his own list.
activeOn: { machine, since } says which computer is working an item right now —
'laptop' or 'desktop', from the date given. Mike's instruction, 2026-09-03, after item
4.54 was built on both machines in the same week. Absent means nobody is on it. The
page shows it as a column, the control shows it on the row, and the control's save
carries it through. Shutdown clears or keeps it; startup reports the other machine's.
rankedByMike: false marks an item filed after orderedByMikeOn that Mike has not yet
placed. The page and the Handbook control show it. It clears itself: the control's
export does not carry the field, so his next saved list drops it.
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
KIND — 'defect' or 'feature', and it is a GATE, not a label. A defect is something
that already exists being wrong, missing, unverified or unmaintainable. A feature is a
new capability, page, screen or behaviour. tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js FAILS THE BUILD
on a feature whose askedBy.ours is true — a new thing nobody outside asked for cannot be
filed at all. A defect we found ourselves still can, because Mike never asked us to stop
reporting bugs; he asked us to stop inventing work.
REF — A WHOLE NUMBER IS A SUBJECT, ITS DECIMALS ARE THE JOBS IN IT. Mike's ruling,
2026-09-15: 7 is the AI advisory engine, so 7.1/7.2/7.3 are engine jobs and NOTHING
else may start with 7. A new job on an existing subject takes the next free decimal of
that parent; a job belonging to no subject is a new parent, and that is a real event.
The ten parents, and the 2026-09-15 renumber, are design/ITEM-NUMBERING.md.
TAKE A NEW NUMBER FROM `npm run check:branch`, NEVER from this file. It reads every
machine's branch; this file is one branch's view and cannot see the other's. Guessing
produced ELEVEN duplicated refs - 4.81, 4.88-4.92 and 4.94 each name two unrelated
jobs in the archive, where the uniqueness guard below does not reach.
2.x, 3.x, 4.x and 5.1-5.5 ARE CLOSED FAMILIES - the old flat scheme, frozen as history
because 613 references to those numbers are written into 279 code files. Never reissue
one, and never renumber one.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.

items.risk: NO CODE IS OUTSTANDING. TWO non-coding gates stand before a first real recording: the staff consultation, and a lawyer per market - which no longer waits on anything. The declaration gate is built and live since 4.83 closed, so a firm that has not declared cannot start.

items.name: Learning from outcomes across consenting firms - the platform gets smarter with use
items.why: Case reviews already record how each template landed, and the engine reads that back for the same client only. Pooled across firms that consent, anonymised, it can adjust recommendations for everyone.
items.risk: Without it the product cannot honestly claim to get smarter with use beyond one client. The counter-risk is privacy: identifiers or client words leaving a firm, or a firm that never consented being changed by others' outcomes - both refused by the spec.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-10 - 'build a prompt to develop the task to enable real machine learning - such that it does, indeed, get smarter with use. Not just from one firm, but from all those who consent to help develop the model by sharing anonymised data'.

items.name: Wages/Salary Review - labour margin, and a register gated on due diligence
items.why: Mike asked for the wages workbook built into the performance-report section. It is the largest source model in the library: two operating bases, a hiring plan, and twelve months of labour margin projected against actual.
items.risk: Nine decisions stand before any code and eight are Mike's. The register holds a client's named employees with pay, leave and service, so it is the only model touching identifiable people - built ungated it becomes a standing rating of someone's colleagues. And 1,778 of the workbook's cells are typed: any shipped as a constant silently removes the control the model exists to give.

items.name: Load a payroll report to pre-fill the team
items.why: Mike asked for a payroll report to be loadable so an advisor does not type a whole team by hand into step 1 of the Wages/Salary Review.
items.risk: Without it a 29-person team is typed by hand, which is the slowest part of the model and the easiest place to mistype a pay rate. The counter-risk is privacy: a payroll export carries IRD numbers, bank accounts, addresses and dates of birth, none of them needed, so the reader must take its columns and discard the rest at the door and never store the file.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-14 - 'lets explore having the ability to load a payroll report to speed up the process of loading data on the team', then ruled as decision 4. Kept as its own item on his instruction of 2026-09-14.

items.touches: server/report/intake/supportedPackages.js and a new reader beside it, components/WagesTeam.vue (the pre-fill target), and design/mockups/wages-model.html decision 4.
items.note: A PRE-FILL INTO THE TYPED TEAM SCREEN, NEVER AN ALTERNATIVE ROUTE IN - Mike's decision 4, 2026-09-14. A payroll report knows what a person COSTS but can never know the charge-out rate or the daily production efficiency, and the margin is charge rate minus pay rate, so a standalone import would finish and leave a model that cannot compute its own answer. BLOCKED ON MIKE: per supportedPackages.js no package may be called supported until a REAL export has been read. Kept as its own item so it does not close with 5.1.

items.name: The AI declares its model choice only sometimes, so declines under-count
items.why: The marker that records a decline is written about one time in six. Where the AI names a model the page-path scan catches it; a decline has no other source.
items.risk: The declines band on the Model Choices screen under-counts and nothing on it says so, so a mentor reads nine where there were thirty. That band is the gap map - where advisers keep arriving and finding nothing - so an under-count points the next model at the wrong place. Named models are unaffected: their rows come from the exact page-path scan.

items.note: NOT SESSION WORK - MIKE'S RULING, 2026-09-16: it corrects a counter on an internal screen and changes nothing an advisor or a client sees, so it waits until the Model Choices screen has real use behind it. items.name: The right calculator is offered only sometimes, and sometimes the wrong one is
items.why: Measured over 30 live calls: the template choice is right every run, but the calculator paired with it varies - 1, 2 or 3 times in 6 on identical questions, and the wrong budget model 4 times in 6.
items.risk: An advisor asking the same question twice gets different tools, and each answer reads perfectly well alone - so neither they nor UAT can see it. Twice the AI attached the wrong calculator to a correct template, including the wrong size of budget model, which the list forbids in capitals. Sales Dashboard is named correctly but gives no link to click 5 times in 6.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-16 - Mike asked for it to be checked now after a lease-vs-buy miss surfaced during item 7.8's testing; he said yes to filing what the check found. A defect we found, not a feature nobody asked for.

items.touches: data/report-model-summaries.json, whose instruction[] block IS the HOW TO USE THIS LIST rules - edit the rules there, not in code; server/utils/reportModels.js formatReportModelsForPrompt, which only renders that block into the 51,072-character prompt and holds no rule text itself; data/prompts/discover.txt STEP 1, which frames the calculator as an optional extra; and whatever measurement proves a change, which has to be live conversations.
items.note: 🔴 NOT ABSENCE - UNRELIABILITY. The TEMPLATE choice is right every run; the calculator paired with it is what varies. Mike ruled 2026-09-18 that a fitting calculator is ALWAYS offered alongside a template, and the offer rule now names that case - the refusal rule (line 7) is untouched. MEASURED, 6 runs each: Working Capital Cycle 3/6 to 5/6, Sales Dashboard 1/6 to 3/6, links 6/24 to 9/24, substitutions 9 to 6. 8 Levers 0/6 unchanged and NOT a defect. WHAT REMAINS IS THE BUDGET SUBSTITUTION - a separate fault, now item 7.11. Tables in advisory-engine.md P2.
items.comment: 2026-09-16 - filed on Mike's yes. 2026-09-17 - six name collisions found and fixed. 2026-09-18 - re-measured at 6 runs per model, which overturned BOTH earlier readings: 'eight never offered' is really three unreliable plus one non-defect, and the budget wording was tested as the cause and DISPROVED - a distinguishing sentence added to High-Level Budget's useWhen made the substitution WORSE (4/6 to 6/6) and was reverted the same hour. Mike's wording is untouched. WHAT REMAINS NEEDS A DECISION FROM HIM, not a bench: when should a calculator accompany a template that already answers the question?

items.name: A budget question is answered with the wrong size of budget model
items.why: Asked whether a client is hitting their budget, the AI offers the Mid-Level Budget's page 5 times in 6 and the High-Level Budget's own page once - the near-miss substitution the instruction block forbids outright.
items.risk: The advisor opens a cashflow-timing model to answer a did-we-hit-target question, and finds out in front of their client. It is the exact consequence the refusal rule describes. UAT cannot catch it: the answer names the right template first and reads perfectly well, and the same question answers differently run to run.

items.name: The sharing tab says on and off at once with no pool secret
items.why: A firm whose switch is on, on a server with no pool secret, sees a green 'Sharing since' badge and a count of adjustments applying, directly beside a notice saying shared learning is switched off.
items.risk: The manager cannot tell which is true. Both numbers are stale: the consent is real but nothing is pooling, and the adjustment count was computed when the pool was readable. No data is at risk and the engine is correct - only the screen misleads.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-15 - found while building Mike's warn-never-block ruling, by reading the screen that ruling put the notice on. A defect we found; filed rather than fixed because nobody asked for it.

items.touches: components/firm/FirmOutcomeConsent.vue - the pillOn badge and the 'What sharing has changed for your advisors so far' card, both of which should defer to poolConfigured. server/routes/outcomeConsent.js computes adjustmentsApplying only when consent is on.
items.note: GIVE-TO-GET IS ALREADY BUILT AND GUARDED - IT IS NOT THE FAULT AND MUST NOT BE REOPENED. Mike ruled it 2026-09-15, 'they contribute to receive'; loadPooledForSession returns adjustments:[] for a firm that does not share, and outcomeLearningTrace.test.js pins all three ways to not-share with 'the pool is never read'. An earlier note here claimed the opposite, misreading a count that is only computed when the switch is ON. The fix is the two stale figures on the screen, nothing in the engine.
items.comment: 2026-09-15 - filed after a wrong reading was corrected against the code: the dev firm was sharing when the '2 adjustments' was seen, so it was never evidence of a non-sharing firm receiving anything.

items.name: A page's templates are hidden behind whichever won the ID
items.why: A page often holds several templates, so 220 client tools sit on 205 pages. One shared profile per page is correct, but the registry keeps only the first template on each page, hiding the other 15 from anything reading it.
items.risk: Nothing scores wrongly and no advice is withheld: the resolver filters the full 220-row array and never keys by page, so every tool competes. The loss is visibility - a profile screen, an audit or a count reading the registry sees 205 titles and cannot name the 15 tools sharing those pages, so a mentor editing a page's profile is not told which tools it governs.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-16 - told us the relationship is one-to-many by design, 'a single page will contain multiple templates which is why this occurs', and said to save it as a job and move around it.

items.touches: server/utils/templateRegistry.js, the page-to-entry Map that keeps one template per page; scripts/build-semantic-profiles.js, which writes one row per page and names only the winner; US9's template-profile screen in 7.2, which must list every template on a page.
items.note: THE SHARED PROFILE IS RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED' - Mike ruled 2026-09-16 that templates on one page SHARE one AI profile, because an advisor opening that page gets them all. This is not a rekey. What is missing is the many half: the registry should carry every template on a page, so a screen can show that this profile governs both Working Capital Cycle and Activity Ratios. Collisions grew 10 to 14 between the 25 June and 30 July exports, so more tools hide as the library grows. NEVER EDIT THE IDS - CLAUDE.md.
items.comment: 2026-09-16 - found while running T060a for 7.2 US9; the compiler appeared to discover six new tools that were only collision winners changing places. Filed first as a keying defect, then corrected twice by Mike: the one-to-many page relationship is by design, and one shared profile per page is the behaviour he wants. RENUMBERED 7.5 to 7.10 on Mike's ruling of 2026-09-16: the laptop had taken 7.5 the same day for the model-choice record, and a number is spent for good once used.

items.name: A working-tree Handbook preview can be published over the shared link
items.why: npm run handbook --working-tree builds a preview of one machine's uncommitted branch. Nothing stops that file being published to the shared URL, so the page Mike opens can show one division's work in progress instead of the agreed origin/master build.
items.risk: The page stops being the same for both machines, which is the one guarantee item 4.85 was built to give. A reader cannot tell a preview from the shared page without noticing the banner, and features present on the OTHER branch vanish from the index while it is live. Nothing is lost from git - the Briefs stay committed on their own branch - but the front door silently describes a state neither master nor the other machine is in.

askedBy.detail: 2026-09-17 - found at desktop shutdown when a publish was refused: the live Handbook was a laptop working-tree preview, 47 pages, its own banner reading "a preview, not the shared page". Mike said yes to filing it. A defect we found, not a feature nobody asked for.

items.touches: scripts/build-handbook.js --working-tree and its WORKING_TREE banner, which are correct and stay; the publish step of .claude/commands/startup.md, which is where the guard belongs because the script cannot know where its output is sent; design/features/handbook.md.
items.note: THE FLAG IS NOT THE FAULT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED - a preview of your own branch is useful and it labels itself honestly. The gap is that nothing refuses to PUBLISH one to the shared URL. Cheapest honest fix: the publish step reads the built file's banner and refuses when it says working tree. Checked 2026-09-17: the only page that differed was strategy-planner, committed and pushed on feat/advisor-progress, so nothing was at risk - it appears on the shared page the day that branch reaches master.
items.comment: 2026-09-17 - Mike ruled the live preview stays rather than being overwritten: it shows one extra real feature and hiding it would gain nothing. This item is about the guard, not about that page.
